<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:ordering}
Let $V_{\mathrm{fix}}$ be the mean reward per round of the best fixed circuit that incurs no detection, $V_\pi$ that of any policy $\pi$ that acts on the observations above and incurs no detection, and $V_{\mathrm{DP}}$ the value of dynamic programming over $s_t$ under the constraint that no trajectory ends in detection. Then, $V_{\mathrm{fix}} \leqslant V_\pi \leqslant V_{\mathrm{DP}}$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
A fixed circuit is a policy that ignores its observations, which gives the first inequality. The drift is Markov and $p_t$ is observed, and detection depends on the trajectory only through $E_T$, so $s_t$ is a sufficient statistic for the constrained problem. Every observation available to $\pi$ is a function of the history, and a history-dependent policy is dominated in a finite-horizon Markov decision process by the optimal policy over a sufficient state~\cite{puterman1994mdp}, which gives the second inequality.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
